title: U.S. Senate · Oregon

context.text: Incumbent Jeff Merkley defeated Paul Damian Wells 93.2%-6.2% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. David Brock Smith, a sitting Oregon state senator, won a seven-candidate Republican primary with 29.5% of the vote, ahead of Jo Rae Perkins (27.1%) and Brent Barker (23.3%). Gary Dye is the Libertarian Party nominee and Chris Henry is the Pacific Green Party and Progressive Party nominee.

summary.text: Jeff Merkley is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election to the U.S. Senate seat he has held since 2009. He previously served in the Oregon House of Representatives.

background.text: Born in Myrtle Creek, Oregon; earned a bachelor's degree from Stanford University and a master's degree from Princeton University.
Elected to the Oregon House of Representatives in 1998 and served from 1999 until his election to the U.S. Senate in 2008.

priorities.text: Describes his role as fighting to restore the American Dream and standing up for middle-class families, focused on equal opportunity for children and a fair shot for people who work hard, 'no matter where they started in life.'
Lists agriculture, health care, jobs and the economy, natural resources and rural development, consumer and taxpayer protection, and tackling climate change among his issue priorities.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Chemical Safety, Waste Management, Environmental Justice, and Regulatory Oversight), the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on Appropriations (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies), the Committee on Rules and Administration, and is Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on the Budget.

summary.text: David Brock Smith is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate. He is a sitting Oregon state senator who previously served in the Oregon House of Representatives.

background.text: Born in Port Orford, Oregon; earned an associate degree from Southwestern Oregon Community College and Southern Oregon University; worked in the culinary industry.

Served as Port Orford City Council president and president of the local chamber of commerce before being elected to the Oregon House of Representatives in 2016; has served in the Oregon State Senate since 2023, succeeding Dallas Heard, and was elected to a full term in that seat in 2024.

record.text: As an Oregon state legislator, served on the House and Senate Natural Resources and Wildlife Recovery, Agriculture and Natural Resources, and Energy and Environment committees across multiple sessions (2017-2024), including as vice chair of the House Energy and Environment Committee (2021-2022).

candidates.name: Gary Dye

summary.text: Gary Dye is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. Senate. He is a chemical/gas measurement engineer and has run for office in Oregon in multiple previous cycles.

background.text: Born in Portland, Oregon; earned degrees from Oregon State University, Pepperdine University (bachelor's and MBA), and the University of California, Irvine.
Worked as a chemical engineer and gas measurement engineer in the natural gas and oil-refining industries; has served on the board of directors of the Libertarian Party of Oregon.

candidates.researchNotes: Dye has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no 2026 campaign website or statements were found; background is drawn from Ballotpedia biography and an earlier (2024) survey response not reused here for positions.

candidates.name: Chris Henry

summary.text: Chris Henry is the Pacific Green Party and Progressive Party nominee for U.S. Senate. He has a background in union and community advocacy work.

background.text: Graduated from a UAW trade school in 1985; career experience includes work as a community advocate, union truck driver, and aircraft mechanic.
